widgets_values:
# Run Photoshop Action — read this before you queue

This node opens the image in Photoshop, **plays one of your saved Actions on it
automatically**, and hands the result back. No clicking, no waiting on you.

## Fill in the two blank fields first

They ship empty on purpose — an Action name we invented wouldn't exist on your
machine. Queue this as-is and there is nothing for it to run.

- **`action_name`** — the Action's name, typed **exactly** as it appears in
  Photoshop's Actions panel. Capitals, spaces, brackets and all.
- **`action_set`** — the folder that Action lives in, again exactly.

If your Actions panel still has Photoshop's stock set loaded, try
`Sepia Toning (layer)` in `Default Actions` as a first test.

## Two things that will bite you

1. **This one genuinely needs the Photoshop panel plugin.** There's no
   file-only fallback, because only the plugin can reach Photoshop's Actions
   panel. If the plugin isn't installed and connected, this node can't work —
   every other node in this pack has a plugin-free path, this one doesn't.

2. **Turn off every "show dialog" toggle inside the Action.** That's the little
   square next to a step in the Actions panel. Leave one switched on and
   Photoshop stops on a dialog box waiting for a human — your run just sits
   there until `timeout_seconds` runs out.

The run blocks while the Action plays, so keep `timeout_seconds` comfortably
longer than the Action actually takes. 1800 is half an hour.

## What to try

Point **Load Image** at something of your own, run a colour-grade Action on it,
then swap `action_name` for a different one and queue again. The **Save Image**
node writes each result to `ComfyUI/output/` prefixed `photoshop_action`, so you
can line them up afterwards.
